Sonne Finance is a Compound v2 fork on Optimism that was vulnerable to the classic first-depositor share-inflation attack, made possible by precision loss in integer arithmetic. The attacker first executed five previously-queued timelock governance proposals to list VELO as a new collateral market (soVELO) with a very small initial exchange rate. Using a flash loan of ~35.5M VELO from the Velodrome AMM, the attacker minted only 400,000,001 wei of soVELO (creating a near-zero total supply), then immediately donated ~35.5M VELO directly to the soVELO contract. This massively inflated the per-share exchange rate: exchangeRate = (totalCash + totalBorrows - totalReserves) / totalSupply. With totalSupply at 400,000,001 wei and totalCash inflated by 35M VELO, each soVELO share represented enormous underlying value. The attacker entered the market with soVELO as collateral and borrowed 768,947 USDC. Due to truncation (precision loss) in the redeemUnderlying calculation, the attacker was then able to redeem totalCash - 1 worth of VELO back from the contract, repaying the flash loan and netting both the borrowed USDC and a large share of the donated VELO. Based on Compound's Optimism native lending protocol, Sonne Finance has fallen victim to a lightning loan attack by hackers, resulting in losses exceeding $20 million USD.

Sonne Finance lost roughly $20 million on Optimism in May 2024 after an attacker exploited a newly activated VELO lending market. The attacker inflated the market’s exchange rate through direct token donations to an almost empty Compound V2 style market, then used rounding behavior in redeemUnderlying to borrow against overstated collateral and drain assets from other pools. Sonne Finance suffered a $20 million exploit on Optimism in May 2024 after a new VELO market was enabled as collateral. The attacker manipulated the market's exchange rate by donating tokens to an empty pool, then exploited rounding errors in the protocol's Compound v2 fork code to drain collateral assets across multiple lending pools. Sonne Finance's governance added a VELO market with collateral enabled before seeding sufficient initial supply. The attacker, being the first supplier, donated a large amount of VELO directly to the soVELO contract, inflating the exchange rate. The Sonne Finance lending protocol was exploited for at least $20 million as an attacker was able to exploit a vulnerability in some of their smart contracts . Sonne is a fork of the Compound Finance project, which has known vulnerabilities that are sometimes not properly addressed by people who reuse the code — as has happened with Radiant Capital and Rari . After being alerted to the theft by several security companies, Sonne announced they had paused the contract on the Optimism Ethereum layer-2 chain.
